page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For storage, the instance is bundled with 1890 GB of local disk capacity and supports Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in text processing, image processing, and Passmark CPU encryption. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark memory scores also fall into the top tier. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, memory bandwidth (both cached small block and uncached large block), and database operations on Passmark register in the average tier.

The D32ads_v6 is configured for workloads requiring a balance of compute and memory, such as web serving, software compilation, and text processing. Its 1890 GB local storage makes it viable for database operations, though its database benchmark scores remain in the average tier. For machine learning, the instance shows strong prompt processing and text generation speeds for small LLM models, but drops to average performance for medium and large models. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a standard resource density, offering a balanced hardware profile without the high cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances.
